title: 02 — Databricks Engineer Track
html:
02 — Databricks Engineer Track

The one idea: a Databricks engineer owns the platform others build on: the catalog and its permissions, the compute and its cost, the pipelines and jobs, deployment, sharing and the AI services. Complete the data engineer's Level 1 first, then go deep on the platform.

1. Level 1: Foundation

Complete Data Engineer Track, Level 1, including all eight hands-on labs. Then read the Databricks Platform chapter.

Checklist:

  • I can explain the control plane vs the compute plane, and serverless vs classic compute.
  • I can create a catalog, schema, volume and table, and grant access to a group.

2. Level 2: Practitioner

Read, in order Hands-on
Unity Catalog in Depth Grants with inheritance, a column mask, a row filter, and a query on system.access.audit
Lakeflow: Connect, Pipelines and Jobs A pipeline with expectations and AUTO CDC to SCD2. A job with a file arrival trigger and a condition task
Delta Lake MERGE, time travel, OPTIMIZE, VACUUM
Databricks SQL, Compute and Performance A serverless warehouse, liquid clustering, a query profile read
PySpark Cookbook Rewrite one SQL pipeline in PySpark

Project: one bundle (databricks.yml) that deploys a pipeline, a job and permissions to dev and prod targets from CI.

Checklist:

  • Nothing in my project was created by clicking. Everything is deployed from the bundle.
  • I can explain why a user gets "permission denied", from the grants alone.
  • My pipeline's expectations and their metrics are visible.

3. Level 3: Professional

Read, in order Hands-on
Iceberg Anatomy, Deletes and v3, Catalogs Read a UC table from PyIceberg or DuckDB through the REST endpoint
Sharing and Collaboration A share to an open recipient, then revoke it
The Databricks AI Stack ai_parse_document on a PDF in a volume, and a hybrid search index
Lakebase and Databricks Apps A small review app writing decisions to Lakebase
Contracts, Lineage and Observability Lineage and billing queries on system tables
CI/CD & Azure: Entra ID, Key Vault, storage Service principals, secret scopes, storage credentials

Project: a cost and governance report built from system tables. It shows cost per job and per team, unused tables, and tables without owners. It runs as a job and feeds a dashboard.

Checklist:

  • I can show what each job and warehouse cost last week.
  • Every production job runs as a service principal, with secrets from Key Vault.
  • Access to sensitive columns is by governed tag and ABAC policy, not per table.
  • An outside engine can read a governed table without long-lived keys.

4. Level 4: Senior

  • Platform design: workspaces and catalogs per environment and team, network isolation, identity federation, disaster recovery.
  • Cost governance: budgets, policies, serverless vs classic decisions, predictive optimization, and chargeback.
  • Change management: track What's New 2026 and the Databricks release-notes feed (news sources). Plan migrations off deprecated features, such as Hyperopt, legacy inference tables and Foundation Model Fine-tuning.
  • Security: securing agents and MCP tools, and personal data.

Checklist:

  • I have written the platform's environment, identity and catalog design.
  • We have a deprecation register with dates and owners.
  • Cost per product is reported every month, and it is trending the right way.
